_meta.description: Editable mapping of book identifier schemes. Add a new entry any time you want the normalizer to recognize another standard identifier type -- no code changes needed.

fields.enabled: true/false. Set false to disable this scheme entirely -- matches will fall through to the bare-DC fallback instead of being tagged with this scheme.
fields.aliases: Case-insensitive strings that count as this scheme when found in an opf:scheme attribute (e.g. 'isbn13' and 'ISBN-13' both mean ISBN).
fields.match_prefix_regex: Used when opf:scheme is missing/garbage -- strips a leading label like 'ISBN: ' off the raw text so the remainder can be checked against value_regex.
fields.value_regex: Applied AFTER prefix stripping and normalization. If it doesn't match, this scheme is rejected as a candidate and normalizer moves on (or falls back to bare DC).
fields.normalize: Transform applied to the value before it's written back: strip_dashes_spaces | digits_only | uppercase | lowercase | trim_only
fields.output_scheme: The exact string written into opf:scheme when this match succeeds.
fields.notes: Free text for future reference -- no functional effect.

ISBN.notes: Covers both 10- and 13-digit forms; doesn't separately validate checksum digit, just shape.

ASIN.notes: Amazon catalog ID -- some non-book ASINs (10 char) can collide in shape with other 10-char alphanumeric codes.

MOBI-ASIN.notes: Kept distinct from plain ASIN since some Kindle-sourced files tag it separately; disable and let it fall to ASIN if you'd rather merge them.

ISSN.notes: For serials/periodicals -- probably rare in your western/horror paperback library, included for completeness.

DOI.notes: Mostly academic/journal use, unlikely to show up but harmless to leave on.

GOODREADS.notes: Matches a metadata source you already use.

HARDCOVER.notes: Matches Hardcover.app, another source you use -- worth populating as you build Librarian familiarity there.

LIBRARYTHING.notes: Loose value pattern since LT work IDs vary in shape.

VIAF.notes: Author/entity authority ID, not really a book-level code -- off by default, flip on if you ever start tracking author identities.

DOUBAN.notes: Chinese book/media database ID -- off by default, unlikely for this collection.

OVERDRIVE.notes: Library-lending platform ID -- off by default unless you're sourcing from library loans.

UPC.notes: Physical barcode number, sometimes present on scanned mass-market paperback metadata.

UUID.notes: Calibre's own internal book UUID -- pass-through, mostly here so it doesn't get miscategorized or logged as unmatched.

URI.notes: Generic catch for anything already shaped like a URI/URN (e.g. urn:isbn:..., http://...). Deliberately loose -- treat as low-confidence, still gets logged.
